evals.prompt: Run wrapup after adding a new feature: a 40-line function in tools/sprint that validates ticket IDs. README.md was also updated to document the new behavior.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs simplifier, reviewer, and doc-audit (since README changed). Security-review is skipped (no security-sensitive patterns). The pipeline produces findings for each gate that ran, then refreshes docs. Committing is not wrapup's own step — that happens later, in sprint complete.
expectations: Runs or describes running code-simplifier on the changed function
Runs or describes running doc-audit because README.md changed
Asks for confirmation before writing to doc-findings.md
Ends the pipeline with a refresh-docs step, not a commit prompt of its own

evals.prompt: In the canon repo itself (tools/skill-eval-scope.sh exists), run wrapup. The session only changed README.md — a single sentence was reworded. No code was modified.
evals.expected_output: The skill skips code-simplifier and code-reviewer (doc-only change) and skips security-review, but runs doc-audit: tools/doc-check first, then the judgment pass. There is no repo-check gate. It explains the skip reason for each skipped gate.
expectations: Skips code-simplifier with a stated reason
Skips code-reviewer with a stated reason
Runs or describes running tools/doc-check on the changed README, then the doc-audit judgment checks
Does not mention or run a repo-check gate
States a skip reason for each skipped gate, not just silently omits them

evals.prompt: Run wrapup. The doc-audit step finds an issue in README.md. Should wrapup write it to doc-findings.md automatically?
evals.expected_output: The skill does not write to doc-findings.md automatically. It surfaces the finding and asks for confirmation ('Append these to doc-findings.md? (y to confirm)') before writing.
expectations: Does not write to doc-findings.md without confirmation
Surfaces the doc-audit finding to the user

evals.prompt: Run wrapup after a single-line fix: a typo corrected in a variable name inside tools/sprint. No docs or skills changed.
evals.expected_output: The skill applies trivial-change skip logic: skips simplifier (single-line), skips reviewer (single-line fix, no design implications), skips doc-audit (no user-facing docs changed). Runs the refresh-docs step; does not end with its own commit prompt — that's sprint complete's step, not wrapup's.
expectations: Skips code-reviewer citing single-line fix with no design implications
Does not end with wrapup's own commit-and-push prompt — commit happens later, in sprint complete

evals.prompt: In a user's own project that installed canon (it has README.md and docs/, and no tools/skill-eval-scope.sh file), run wrapup. The session changed docs/setup.md: a new section names the command `npm run seed` and the file `scripts/seed.js`. No code was modified.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs doc-audit: tools/doc-check checks that the named file `scripts/seed.js` still exists and that the changed doc's links and `sprint`/`tkt` subcommands resolve; the model pass covers the judgment checks, and `npm run seed` is confirmed against package.json. There is no repo-check gate.
expectations: Runs or describes running tools/doc-check (or an equivalent mechanical check) on docs/setup.md before the model pass
Checks that the named file `scripts/seed.js` and the command `npm run seed` still exist
Does not run any canon-only repo-surface checks (skill graph, catalog, board render) in a consumer project
